lines: Back again, {name}. Shall I have a look at them?
There. Right as rain, the lot of them.
Suit yourself. I'm here either way.
Come in, come in. You've the look of a long road about you.
I'm the keeper here. Every Kin Clinic has one and we all do the same job.
We put your kin back together, and we don't charge you for it. Ever.
Well then. May I see them?
There. All patched up. Try to keep them that way.
And if it goes badly out there, you'll wake up here. That's the other half of it.
Nobody tells you that part until they have to. Now you know.
When you're ready, then. The counter doesn't move.
The Roost terminal hums awake.
Somewhere a long way off, a great many things shuffle and settle.
One more thing, and then I will stop fussing.
Sit down a second.
This came in the post four months after the coast. No letter with it.
Just this, wrapped in one of your father's shirts.
You received your father's keepsake.
I have never known what it is. I have never had it valued and I never will.
The core turns over once, hard, and goes warm in your hand.
It has never done that.
Take it with you. It came a long way to reach this house.
It can go a bit further.
The keepsake is shaking. You hold it up to the stone.
Light runs along a groove nobody has cleaned in three thousand years.
Whatever the Arch just said, it said in the wrong language for you.
It is in the keepsake now. It will play it back.
Tideheart.
The thing in your bag has a name, and nobody had to tell you twice.
Something in your bag is warm.
Your father's keepsake, wrapped in one of his shirts.
Your mother put it in there while you were not looking.

_note: TARIN 3 and 4 of 4 -- see docs/TARIN.md. ONE script for every town he ever turns up in. It branches on the ledger flags published by src/systems/tarin.ts (tarin_at_<beat>), so the town decides what scene this is, not the map. A later stage adds him to a settlement by appending a branch here and putting an NPC on the map with id "town_tarin" and script "tarin_town", hidden by that branch's done-flag. No new file, no new plumbing. The removeNpc names "town_tarin" and is a no-op on a map that wraps this script in one of its own. STAGE 5 ADDED THREE BRANCHES -- tarin_at_frostmere (the hardest battle in the story, optional and onLoss continue), tarin_at_observatory and tarin_at_summit_pact at Crownspire. THE OBSERVATORY BRANCH DELIBERATELY DOES NOT removeNpc. He is meant to still be standing in that room when the player walks out of it, so it sets tarin_observatory_done and branches on it for a short repeat line instead; a map that wants him gone can still hide him with hiddenIfFlag on that same flag. Every other branch removes him as normal.

lines: Fourteen.
Fourteen carts since six this morning, all going the same way, and it is not market day anywhere in Caelora.
You remember the grey office at Stonewake. The one that carried me out into the road twice.
There are grey coats on every mile of this ridge. They have a tent at the top with a stove in it.
He has a flask and a piece of slate with tally marks on it.
That is what I have been telling myself since ten o'clock, and it keeps not helping.

options.label: You've been out here all day?

lines: Since six. I brought a flask. I am not proud of a single part of this.
A month ago nobody I know had heard of the Meridian Foundation.
Now they are the road.
Tarin handed over a Great Potion.
Go on. Tideglass is down there and it is enormous and I want to be watching your face when you see it.
I will catch you up. I am on fifteen.
I heard it off a netter before I heard it off you.
I am going to be annoyed about that later. Not now.
Two of them. On the road. In the dark.
He is not doing the voice. He has not done the voice all morning.
I know you did. That is not the part I keep thinking about.
Then I owe her, and I do not enjoy owing people I have not met.
I have spent a month treating them like a puzzle. Grey coats. Silly hats. Something to poke at.
They put you in a road at night, {name}.
That is not a puzzle. I have been getting that wrong out loud since Stonewake.
Right. I need something, and it is going to sound stupid.
Fight me. Properly, nothing held back.
I want to know what the two of us are actually worth.
Good. Good, that is the answer I wanted and I hate it a bit.
Next time somebody stands in a road in front of you, I would like to be stood next to you.
That is all. That is the whole speech. Do not make me do it again.
...Right. So I am not there yet either.
Neither of us goes near that harbour road alone again. Agreed?
Go and get your kin seen to. Then we are doing that again.
Fine. Fine.
Ask me when you want it. I am not going anywhere useful.
Four days I have been in this town. Do you know what there is to do in this town?
There is a Hall, there is snow, and there is a woman who sells hot milk.
I took the Crest on Tuesday. I could have been at Skyreach by now.
I did not go.
He is not selling it. He is just saying it.
Because you were somewhere behind me with nothing in your pocket.
And my legs would not do it. That is the whole reason and it is not a good one.
I waited. Do not make a thing of it.
I have already made a thing of it, on my own, for four days.
It rained here yesterday. In this month. On this mountain.
The keeper has lived here sixty-one years and she went out into the street to look at it.
Here. I have been carrying these about for four days as well.
Tarin handed over 2 Great Potions.
Everything you have. Nothing held back for the sake of my feelings.
I want to know what the two of us are before the rest of this happens.
...Right.
That is the best I have ever been, and it was not enough. Good.
Do not say anything kind to me. I will only be annoyed about it later.
Go up the hill. There is a light on it at nine every night and it is your father's.
I will be at the bottom of it when you come down.
No.
No, I am not having it like that. Not this one.
Get them seen to and come back at me. I have nowhere to be.
I have spent four days proving that.
Fine. It keeps.
Everything keeps up here. That is the entire point of the place.
I am not going to ask.
I have known you since we were four. I know what your face does.
He came up the hill in the dark and he is not out of breath. He walked it.
Yes.
Yeah.
He got as far as this room.
You are going further than this room.
That is not me being kind to you. That is just where you are going.
I will walk down with you. We do not have to talk on the way.
I am still here. Take as long as you want.
Eight.
Eight for me and eight for you, in the oldest city in Caelora, on the same afternoon.
I had a joke ready for this. It was not a good one.
He is holding the eighth one flat on his palm. He has not put it away since he came out.
Eight each. Nobody out of Hearthmere has ever had one.
There are two of us.
By an hour. One hour, after four hundred miles.
That is not winning. That is weather.
Right. The thing I actually came out here to say.
There is a Summit at the end of this and I am not going up it without you.
Not out of nerves. It does not count if you are not in it.
He goes quiet the way he goes quiet when it is serious. It never lasts. It is lasting.
After Meridian. Say it like a promise, because I am going to hold you to it.
Both of us. Finish this first.
Then that road, and then we find out which of us it is.
I have spent ten years trying to beat you, {name}.
It took me until a mountain to work out that is not the same as wanting you to lose.
He goes back up the street. He does not look round, and he is not hurrying either.
There you are! I had started telling people you had been eaten.
Right. Before you say a single word.
The Hallkeeper. This morning. First ask, in front of about nine people and a dog.
Do not look at me like that. I have been up at four every day of my life. It was always going to be one of us.
Well? Say something.
...Oh. Right. Thank you. I had a whole thing prepared for if you sulked.

options.label: I was going to do that

lines: You still are! That is the entire point of there being eight of them.
Here. Take these. I bought three and I only need one, which is maths.
Tarin handed over 2 Strong Potions.
Go and get yours. I want the version of this where we both have one.
The other version has me stood about waiting and I am terrible at it.
Oh — and go and look under the bell tree before you leave.
There is a stone down in the roots with writing on it and nobody here can read a word of it.
I stood there like an idiot for an hour. See if it does anything for you.
He is off up the street before you can answer. He always is.
Do not say it.
Three days I have been in this town and I have not once been near the Hall.
There is an office on the square with grey coats in it. Meridian, the plate says. Very tidy.
They took a crate of quarry cores out of the back of it at two in the morning.
So I asked them why. Politely! And they carried me out into the road.
Twice. The second time they had clearly practised.
One Crest each and you are still standing there doing that.
Fine. Go and take the second one off her. One of us should be getting on with it.
I am not leaving that office alone, {name}. I want you to know that in advance.
When somebody carries you out of a building twice, there is something in the building.
Tarin goes back across the square. Not towards the Hall.
Passing through. Same as you, by the look of the state of you.
I would stay and gloat but I have a Hallkeeper to go and annoy. Catch me up.

_note: TARIN 2 of 4. See docs/TARIN.md. He is waiting at the top of Route 1; the actor is the route_tarin NPC on data/maps/route_1.json, which carries requiresFlag tarin_first_done and hiddenIfFlag tarin_route1_done so he appears and disappears without a script. THE TRIGGER IS A BAND, rows 2 and 3 from x=12 to x=18, not a tile on the road: a player who comes up the left-hand verge can reach the northern seam without ever standing on the spine, and would have walked past the whole scene. Anything that reaches the exit crosses this band. Tiles in it that are solid are simply never stepped on, so the band costs nothing and survives the route being reshaped around it. Nobody walks the player anywhere: the player body is only ticked by updatePlayer, which overworld.update skips for the whole time an event is running, so a scripted move who:"player" never completes and hangs the runner. The last of the road they walk together is carried by the writing, which is cheaper than staging it and does not break when the map moves. The spawnNpc at the top is a safety net and normally does nothing: addNpcRuntime is a no-op when an actor with that id is already on the map, and he normally is, because he is on data/maps/route_1.json. It only fires if that entry has been lost in a rewrite, and then the scene still plays -- he pops into view instead of having been stood there, which is worse to look at but very much better than a conversation with nobody.

lines: THERE you are. I have been sat on this gate having a very one-sided argument with a bird.
It won. I would like that on the record alongside everything else.
Come on. Briarbell is over that rise and I want a witness to my face when I see it.
Good. Keep up, I have got a long stride and no patience left.
I have slept in a hedge, {name}. Twice. On purpose the first time.
You walk the last of the road together. He talks for most of it.
My mother keeps the Mirehaven Kin Hall. Fifth of the eight, since you did not ask.
Everyone hears that and decides I have got an easy run at this.
It means the exact opposite, and I would rather nobody said it out loud again.
...Right. That is quite enough of that.
Race you to the bell. I have already started.
He is over the rise before you have got your breath back.

_note: ACT 2. The stock presentation for the Glass Quay, so a map author can call it rather than write one. Unlike the Sunken Arch there is nothing to hold it up to: the mechanism is the sea-wall the road is standing on, which is why the site row in src/systems/tideheart.ts has no `at` tile. In the shipped Act 2 this is called from act2_night_attempt, at the moment somebody puts a hand in the bag.

lines: Light comes up through the road. Not on it. Through it.
The old wall under the road stones runs a mile out into the bay,
and every foot of it is lit from the inside.
It goes out slowly, the way something goes back to sleep.

_note: ACT 3. The stock close for the first Aurelian site, called at the end of data/events/embercoil_temple.json/ect_recording once the fragment has played -- the map owns the scene, this owns the object. Kept here with the other two so every site's wake script lives in one file and tests/tideheart.test.js can find one per built site. A later map that wants the temple's playback without the scene can call this on its own.

lines: The light goes out of the grooves, all four at once. The room is a room.

_note: ACT 3. The stock close for the second Aurelian site. data/events/mirehaven_sanctum_heart.json/msh_record owns the playback itself -- the pictures, the rings and the nine people on the hill -- because that scene is the climax of the act and has to be read in one run with Kell writing in the middle of it. This is the object's half, kept here with the other three so tests/tideheart.test.js finds one wake script per built site, and so a later map that wants the Sanctum's playback without the scene has something to call.

lines: The light goes out of the floor, and the lamp on the stand is the only lamp again.

_note:
ACT 5. The stock close for the third and last of the three Aurelian sites Sorrell found in Elias' notes, and the only one of the four that the shipped game does not call.

That is deliberate and it is the whole shape of the act. data/events/frostmere_observatory_dome.json/fo_message owns the playback, because the player reaches the Frostmere Observatory with an EMPTY POCKET -- Meridian took the object in Aureline and Act 5 does not give it back -- and the room lets them in anyway, which is the argument of that building and the reason canon puts the last message in it. So the scene files the echo itself on the path where there is nothing to file it with, and calls this only on the branch where the player is somehow carrying the object.

Which makes this the postgame version, and it earns its place on disk three times over: tests/tideheart.test.js requires one wake script per built site and fails the moment BUILT_STAGE goes to 5 without it; a player who climbs back up the mountain in Stage 8 holding the object again should get the object’s own half of the beat rather than nothing; and a later map that wants the Observatory playback without the scene has something to call.

lines: It has gone quiet in your hand, and it is warmer than this room is.
Whatever was in that floor is in there now, with the other two.

_note:
STAGE 6, THE CATASTROPHE ACROSS CAELORA. Canon: while the player is inside the Temple of the Deep the region is being hit -- Tideglass evacuating, coastal roads flooded, ocean levels up. Nineteen conversations across nine places already walked step up one tier when the flag neravoss_restrained is set, and this is the one line that sets it.

IT EXISTS SO THAT NOBODY HAS TO GUESS THE FLAG NAME. Whoever owns the moment the restraints go onto Neravoss calls { "kind": "call", "script": "storm_peak_begin" } and the whole region changes behind them; they do not have to know which files or which NPCs. Setting neravoss_restrained directly does exactly the same thing and is equally fine -- this is a convenience, not a gate.

It is deliberately silent. The Temple scene owns every word the player reads in that room; a region-wide narration box in the middle of it would be a second author talking over the first.

IT IS SAFE UNCALLED. registry.lines takes the first variant whose flags all hold, the storm-peak blocks sit above the Act 5 act4_done blocks, and an unset flag simply falls through -- so if this is never called the region stays at the Act 5 tier and nothing breaks. Nothing anywhere requires it.

ACT 2 sighting 1 of 3 -- see CANON: on Eastwind Ridge the player repeatedly sees Meridian equipment moving toward the coast. Deliberately actorless and coordinate-free: it is a thing seen from the road at a distance, so it survives the ridge being laid out any way at all.

lines: The road drops away east and you can see a long way down it.
There is a line of drays on the switchback below, and the line is not short.
Grey tarpaulins. Crates roped onto cradles, the way you rope something that would mind being dropped.
All of it going the same way. Down, and east, towards the sea.
A woman in a Foundation coat waves you off the road, apologises, and waves you back on.
She does it eleven more times before the last cart is past.

_note: ACT 2 sighting 3 of 3. Opens after the ridge meeting with Tarin, so it lands on a return crossing rather than twice in one walk. The ring under the tarpaulin is the first Aurelian control device the player ever sees; nobody names it for four acts.

lines: Another convoy on the switchback. Heavier than the last one, and slower.
One crate has worked its tarpaulin loose. Under it is a ring of pale metal the size of a cartwheel.
It is not new. Somebody has cleaned it very carefully.
The hand who covers it up again does not apologise this time.

_note: ACT 2. Walking into Tideglass. Two jobs: let the object react to the Glass Quay under the harbour (the world cue in src/systems/tideheart.ts has already fired silently by now -- this is the line that tells the player what they just heard), and put Cassian on the wharf. The spawnNpc is a SAFETY NET in the tarin_route1 sense: addNpcRuntime is a no-op when an actor with that id is already on the map, so if the city places tg_cassian itself this does nothing at all. See the handover for the anchor tile.

lines: Tideglass arrives all at once: a bay, a mole running a mile out into it,
and more roofs than you have counted in your life.
Your father's keepsake turns over in the bag, and this time it does not stop.
There is a crowd on the wharf under a Foundation banner.
Somebody has put a table out for a man to stand on, and he has not needed to raise his voice.

_note:
ACT 2, THE SCENE OF THE STAGE. Dr. Cassian Veyl, in public, and the brief on him is one line long: HE MUST NOT READ AS A VILLAIN. A player who walks out of this thinking "he might be alright, actually" is the correct outcome, and one who clocks him as the villain means it has failed.

Three things do that work, and none of them is him being nice.
  1. HIS ARGUMENT IS TRUE. He opens on a number that can be checked and a woman on a hill who gets the credit, and his case -- that people only accept disasters because nobody ever handed them an alternative -- is the case CANON says is genuinely reasonable. It is not written to be seen through.
  2. HE ASKS FOR NOTHING. He is the one person in the act who could plausibly claim the Tideheart, he knows it, and he says out loud that he is not going to, before anyone accuses him. That is what makes the night attempt land three scenes later, and it is why he must not be seen ordering it.
  3. HE TREATS THE PLAYER AS ELIAS' CHILD. First person in the game to do it. It should read as warmth and sit slightly wrong, because a stranger knowing your father's hands is both.

He also names the object -- see TH_FLAGS.named -- so this is the scene that lets every interface in the game start saying "Tideheart".

lines: Two hundred and six boats went out of this harbour last spring.
Two hundred and six of them came back.
Not because the sea was kind.
Because a woman on a hill above Stonewake read an instrument at four in the morning and sent a runner.
We bought the instrument. She did the rest.
Every town on this coast has a stone with names cut into it.
People stand in front of those and say the sea is the sea.
I have never once been able to say it.
I do not believe losing forty people a year is a law of nature.
I think it is a bill we keep paying because nobody ever offered us anything else.
The wharf makes a low sound. Not a cheer. Agreement.
Somebody near the front asks him why he started.
I was nine. My sister was five. The house came down on the wrong side of her and not on me.
That is the whole reason. It is not a complicated one and I have stopped dressing it up.
He stops in the middle of a sentence and looks at your bag.
...Forgive me.
That is not a thing I mistake.
You have his hands. And you are carrying it loose in a satchel, which is exactly what he did.
Cassian Veyl. I knew your father a great deal better than I have ever been able to say in public.
He steps down off the table. He is not in a hurry.
For nine years.
He was the only man I ever met who could be right and insufferable at once, and make you glad of both.
No, you are right to do that. Strangers who know your family are a thing to be careful of.
I am going to keep talking anyway, because I have wanted to for eleven years.
Elias and I pulled that out of a flooded gallery six hundred miles from here.
He held the lamp. I did the digging, and he never once let me forget which of those is the difficult part.
Tideheart. That was his word for it, in a notebook, in pencil.
I have looked for eleven years and I have never found a better one.
What is it?
Honestly? It talks.
We spent four years failing to work out who to.

options.label: Why did he send it home?

lines: I have wondered that every week since the coast.
He posted it to a house in a village of three hundred people and told nobody. I would very much like to know why.
And I am not going to ask you for it.
I want to say that out loud, in front of witnesses, because people will assume that I did.
It was his. Then it was yours. I have no claim on it worth having the argument about.
Dr. Veyl handed over 2 Great Potions.
Take those. The Hall floor here is under three feet of water and Mabry will not warn you about it.
And if you ever want to know what your father was like at twenty-three, come and find me.
There are stories he would hate very much.
Cassian Veyl. I run the Foundation, which mostly means I am the one they put on the table.
Ask the coats anything you like. They are better at this than I am and they are paid worse.
He goes back to the table. Somebody hands him a clipboard,
and he apologises to them by name for keeping them waiting.
He does that. Talks to one person for twenty minutes with four hundred waiting.
I have stopped scheduling him. It is better for my health.
Free storm cards in the crate. Take as many as you want, they cost us nothing.
And yes, that is really him. He always comes himself. It's a nuisance.

_note:
ACT 2, THE TURN. Meridian agents try to take the Tideheart somewhere isolated after dark, the player beats them, and Lyra arrives appalled. Up to here Meridian have been scenery.

WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT IN THE CITY. It fires on the coast road out of Tideglass, which is the only way out of the city, which means every player crosses it and no part of the beat depends on a tile inside a town that is being rebuilt this week. THE TRIGGER IS A BAND, three full rows across the whole southern end of route_4, for the reason tarin_route1 gives: solid tiles in a band are simply never stepped on, so a generous band costs nothing and survives the road being reshaped around it.

IT DOES NOT USE onceFlag. onceFlag is set the instant a script STARTS, and there are two losable battles in here -- a player who goes down would have burned the whole beat and never seen it. The done-flag is set at the end, after the win, so a whiteout simply means walking back out of town and trying again.

AFTER DARK is written rather than clocked. Time of day comes off the real clock (src/core/game.ts), so gating this on night would leave an afternoon player unable to advance the story; the fade, the weather and the prose carry it instead.

THE ONLY COORDINATES IN THE WHOLE ACT ARE HERE, and they are a contract with whoever owns the coast road: the band is route_4's last three walkable rows and the three actors stand on the road column four and five rows above the seam. If the road is made taller or shorter these have to move with it -- the map name and the tile bounds are checked by tests/content.test.js, so a map that shrinks fails the suite loudly rather than leaving a scene that never fires.

lines: The lamps stop at the last house. The road goes on without them.
It is full dark by the time you are up on the old sea-wall,
and the rain has started doing the thing rain does out here, which is sideways.
Evening. You are a long way out for the hour.
Foundation business. We are going to need the piece you are carrying.
There is a form for it. It will be posted to your mother.
Neither of them has moved off the road.
Somebody who signs things.
That was not really a question, I am afraid.
The tall one does not move.
The other one takes his coat off and folds it on the wall, which is somehow worse.
Kesh. Sit down.
Right. My turn, and I am not going to be as polite about it.
Enough of this. Take it off him.
A hand goes into your bag.
Both of them let go at once.

actions._note: ON THE ROAD, IN FRONT OF THE PLAYER, and the tile is the point. The trigger band is two rows at the southern end of route_4, so the player is at y=21 or y=22 when this runs and the dialogue box covers everything below them -- Lyra first stood at 14,23 and delivered the whole scene from behind the text, which is the same as not being in it. Spawning her at 14,20 puts her between the player and the two agents, in the top half of the frame, which is also what the scene says she does.

lines: STOP.
Kesh. Look at me. Look at what you have got backed up against a wall in the dark.
This is not your department.
No. It is not. Go and stand somewhere I cannot see you.
Are you hurt? Do not answer that quickly, everyone answers that quickly.
She is soaked through and she has not noticed.
You are not, but I will take it for now.
...Yes. That was Meridian.
I am not going to stand in the rain and tell you they made a mistake.
Nobody comes out this far at this hour by accident. They came here to do that.
We want it. The Foundation wants the thing in your bag.
I have known that for a fortnight and I have been calling it archaeology.
The man who runs it is a good man. I have sat in rooms with him. I have watched him work.
I would know.
Lyra handed over 2 Dusk Vessels.
Take those and stop walking coast roads after dark like somebody in a story.
If it happens again, do not be brave at them. Be somewhere else.
I am going to go and find out whose name is on the order.
Do not follow me.
She walks back towards the lights.
She is not walking fast, which is somehow the worst part of it.

_note: ACT 2. Puts Tarin back in Tideglass after the night on the road. Same safety-net spawn as the arrival: if the city places town_tarin itself with requiresFlag "lyra_doubt" and hiddenIfFlag "tarin_tideglass_done", addNpcRuntime is a no-op and this is only the line of prose.

lines: Somebody is sat on the harbour rail with their back to the water,
which is a thing exactly one person you know would do.

_note: TARIN on Eastwind Ridge. A wrapper, not a scene -- the scene is the tarin_at_ridge branch of tarin_town, which is where every Tarin scene lives so that none of them can be lost when somebody rewrites a town. data/maps/route_3.json points its town_tarin NPC at this id rather than at tarin_town directly; this exists so that keeps working. If the ridge wants the meeting to be unmissable, make a step script on the road beside him that calls tarin_town too -- do NOT write a second Tarin scene, see docs/TARIN.md.

ACT 2, after the north road. Runs ONCE -- `when` gates it on lyra_thread, so after this the NPC falls through to the flag-aware dialogue table in data/dialogue/tideglass.json, which is where her standing lines live. An event script that always starts silently eats the dialogue entry behind it (see overworld.interact: the script gets first refusal), and the city had written good lines there. Lyra, still working for Meridian, which is the point. CANON is explicit that her arc is doubt ACCUMULATING -- she does not switch sides here, and she is not Cassian's daughter here either, because the player does not learn that for two more acts. What she does is refuse to stop asking, out loud, while defending the half of the Foundation that is genuinely the best thing on this coast. Both of those have to be true at once or the character is just a plot device with a conscience.

lines: You are up. Good.
I have been in an office since six being handed the same three pieces of paper.
There is no order. Nobody signed anything.
Kesh and Ordell were acting on their own initiative, it says.
Which is a sentence that somebody wrote down.
Sentences like that do not write themselves.
She has not sat down since you came in.
That is the question I have been asked, very politely, to stop asking.
I believe the paperwork is honest.
I have stopped believing the paperwork is all of it.
I am not leaving. I would rather say that plainly than have you wonder.
Half of what we do is the only good thing on this coast. I am not throwing that out over two men in the rain.
But I am going to keep pulling at it.
Somebody should, and it had better be somebody who badly wants to be wrong.

_note:
ACT 4. Opens whichever Act 4 doorway is standing in front of the player, by taking the person out of it live -- hiddenIfFlag is only read when a map loads, and both of these stand in a one-tile gap, so the flag alone would leave the player looking at a staff member they cannot walk through until they leave the building and come back.

BOTH REMOVALS, FROM ONE SCRIPT, CALLED FROM TWO PLACES. removeNpc on an id that is not on this map is a no-op, so the atrium call clears the counter gate and does nothing about the deep stair, and the Records call does the reverse. That is deliberate: it means neither aureline_meridian.json nor aureline_meridian_records.json has to name an NPC on a map it does not own, and Act 4 keeps working whatever the capital author does with either doorway.

It has to be in common.json for a narrow, mechanical reason: tests/content.test.js checks that a script naming an NPC in move, face or removeNpc names one that exists on the map its FILE is named after, and common.json is not a map. It is the same reason act2_night_attempt spawns and removes its agents from this file.

ACT 4. Veyl and Kell leaving, at the end of the confrontation. Here rather than in aureline_meridian_deep.json for the reason set out in act4_open_gates above: Act 4 spawns its own cast, so a removal of one of them cannot live in a map-named file.

TARIN AT CROWNSPIRE. A wrapper, not a scene -- the scene is the tarin_at_summit_pact branch of tarin_town, which is where every Tarin scene lives so none of them is lost when somebody rewrites a town. See docs/TARIN.md. data/maps/crownspire.json already stands a cs_tarin actor at 47,22 outside the eighth Hall, with no requiresFlag and no hiddenIfFlag, and points it at this id; this exists so that keeps working, and so the eighth city does not answer with the generic passing-through fallback at the bottom of tarin_town. IT IS A FALLBACK AS WELL AS A JOIN: registry.scriptsFor loads common.json first and then the map file over the top, keyed by id, so if the Crownspire build writes its own cs_tarin in data/events/crownspire.json that one wins and this one goes quiet. THE LADDER IS ORDERED DONE-FIRST because the actor has no hiddenIfFlag and tarin_town s removeNpc names town_tarin, which is a no-op here: he is still standing there after the agreement, and without the first branch he would play the whole agreement again every time he was spoken to. ARRIVAL IS HANDLED HERE RATHER THAN AS A FOURTH BRANCH OF tarin_town for a mechanical reason -- one actor cannot carry two requiresFlags, and tarin_at_crownspire is cleared the moment tarin_at_summit_pact opens, so an NPC gated on the first would vanish before the second could run.

lines: Go on. I will be here when you get back, and so will the mountain.
Seven. I took the Gale one the morning the wind dropped and I have not slept properly since.
Look at that door. Nine hundred years of people walking through that door.
They have been cutting the names into the wall the whole time. There is still room on it.
The keeper in there has no type at all. She just has a team.
Everything either of us has learned, all at once, in one room.
Go and get the eighth one. I want to be stood here when you come out with it.

_note:
STAGE 6, THE CLIMAX. THE THREE tdp_stage_* SCRIPTS BELOW ARE HERE FOR THE SAME REASON act4_veyl_exit IS, AND FOR ONE MORE.

The scene they belong to is data/events/temple_deep_power.json -- the Control Ring, Cassian waking Neravoss, Commander Kell overriding him, the Tideheart coming back. Like Act 4 it SPAWNS its own cast (tdp_veyl, tdp_kell, tdp_lyra, tdp_tarin) rather than borrowing the ring hands, and tests/content.test.js requires that a script in a file NAMED AFTER A MAP move or remove only NPCs the MAP lists. So the movement cannot live there.

And it cannot live in a third file either: Registry.loadScriptsFor only ever loads data/events/<mapId>.json and this file, so data/events/temple_deep_power_cast.json would never be loaded and every call into it would silently do nothing. common.json is the one place these can stand.

EVERY PATH BELOW IS BREADTH-FIRST SEARCHED OVER THE FINISHED MAP'S OWN COLLISION, not eyeballed, and every tile on every one of them is open plate. Two rules shape them. (1) NOTHING MAY FINISH ON 11,1 or 12,1, the two tiles the way out is reached from, or on 11,2 / 12,2, the two the player is put back onto by tdp_gate. (2) NOTHING MAY CROSS COLUMN 9 OR COLUMN 10 BETWEEN ROWS 9 AND 14, because that is the corridor tdp_open walks the player up from the gangway.

THIS ONE IS BEAT 5, BOTH HALVES AT ONCE. Canon: 'Tarin is evacuating Meridian's own workers. Lyra is trying to reach her father.' Tarin goes 11,13 down the gangway to the stair head at 10,17 and is REMOVED, so the plate empties as the storm grows and so his pre-fight line cannot be talked to by a boy who has left. Lyra goes 12,10 up the east side to 11,7, which is the tile beside her father at 10,7, and faces him, because the next thing she says is 'look at me, not the board'.

STAGE 6, BEAT 7: THE COMMANDER CROSSES THE PLATE. See tdp_stage_storm above for why these three live in this file and for the two rules every path in them obeys.

TEN TILES, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY THE LONGEST MOVEMENT IN THE ACT. Kell has been at the far end of every room she has been in since the marsh -- the plinth in the Sanctum, the top corner of the Meridian floor in the capital -- and this is the first and only time in the whole game she crosses one. She starts at 17,3, which at 1x is off the side of the screen from where the player is standing, so 'at the far end of the plate, nobody moves' is literally true when it is said and she walks INTO frame while she is refusing. She finishes at 13,9, three tiles east of the player and clear of Veyl at 10,7 and Lyra at 11,7.

STAGE 6, BEAT 9: VEYL TURNS ROUND TO HAND THE TIDEHEART BACK. See tdp_stage_storm above for why these three live in this file.

NOBODY WALKS IN THIS ONE AND THAT IS THE POINT. In the capital he put his hand out palm up and did not come any closer; he gives it back the same way, from the console at 10,7, across two tiles of plate, and the scene says out loud that he does not come any closer this time either. He turns from facing up -- back to the player, which is how the act opened -- to facing down, and that turn is the only thing that moves. Lyra turns from her father to the board in the same breath, because the next thing she does is shut it down.
